content:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Rudy Giuliani, who was mayor when the September 11, 2001 attacks took place, were seen shaking hands at a 25th anniversary memorial ceremony in Lower Manhattan on Friday, despite Giuliani never hiding his disdain for New York City's first Muslim mayor.

After Mamdani was elected, Giuliani posted on Facebook implying there could be another 9/11 during his tenure. He also told Newsmax in a Sunday interview that Mamdani should stay away from Friday's commemoration.

“There is no question he should,” Giuliani told the outlet. “I mean, the reality is, that ceremony is for the families of the victims and for Americans to remember this historically.”

“I lost friends there and I know many of the victims' families very well, and the idea of him showing up — I'm offended by it,” Giuliani also said.

Nonetheless, the video below shows Mamdani initiating a greeting with an extended hand to Giuliani. Giuliani initially offered a slight smile, but after a few seconds of conversation, appeared to show displeasure before the two parted ways.

"He came by, we both extended hands of friendship and said hello to each other. I think all of our focus right now should be on the families, on the first responders, being here, hearing the name of every single person taken 25 years ago, and how these families have persevered through the years," Mamdani said.

The Hill noted that Giuliani's reason for wanting Mamdani to skip the event "had to do with Mamdani's faith."

"They very much want to take us over. It's not like 'they just want to be another religion.' They want to dominate us. Mamdani clearly subscribes to that," Giuliani claimed.

Mamdani accused former city leadership of lying to New Yorkers about air quality near the World Trade Center site in the aftermath of the attacks at a City Hall press conference Tuesday, The New York Times reported.

"People got sick because leaders they trusted lied to them and told them it was safe to breathe toxic air," Mamdani said. He added that the number of people who have died from related health issues has surpassed the death toll from the 2001 attacks themselves.
